chunks: And from him, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Saif ibn 'Amirah, from Mansur ibn Hazim, who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) commanded me to recite the two 'Mu'awwidhat' (Surah Al-Falaq and Surah An-Nas) in the written (or recited) prayer.

key_terms.أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdillah, a title for Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him).
key_terms.الْمَكْتُوبَةِ: The written or recited prayer, referring to the portions of the prayer where recitation is obligatory or recommended.
key_terms.الْمُعَوِّذَتَيْنِ: The two 'Mu'awwidhat', referring to Surah Al-Falaq and Surah An-Nas, used for seeking refuge in God.

ai.seo_question: What are the Mu'awwidhat and when should they be recited in prayer according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the specific instruction of Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS) to recite the two 'Mu'awwidhat' (Surah Al-Falaq and Surah An-Nas) within the written portion of the prayer, emphasizing their role in seeking divine protection. In Shia jurisprudence, this underscores the importance of *tawassul* through Quranic verses for spiritual safeguarding during worship, reflecting the Imam's guidance on integrating supplication and recitation. The practice aligns with the broader Shia tradition of utilizing these surahs not merely as recitation but as a means of invoking Allah's refuge from evil influences.
